questions.problem:
$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}, & {x}^{2}\le y\le 1,\,0<x<1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}(1-{x}^{2}), & 0<x<1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $X$ are shown above. Find the expression for the conditional expected value $\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=x]$ for $0<x<1.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional expected value of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

$$
\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=x]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}y.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=x]$ is a function of $x.$ 

The conditional density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3}{2})}{\frac{3}{2}(1-{x}^{2})} \\  & =\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}^{2}\le y\le 1,\,0<x<1.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)=0.$

Therefore, using the definition of the conditional expectation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=x] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}y\cdot \,\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{{x}^{2}}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}[\frac{1}{2}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}\cdot \frac{1-{x}^{4}}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{\cancel{1-{x}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{(1-{x}^{2})}(1+{x}^{2})}{2} \\  & =\frac{1+{x}^{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3(x+y)}{4}, & 0<x\le 2y,\,\,0<y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}3{y}^{2}, & 0<y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the conditional expected value $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=1].$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional expected value of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ is a function of $y.$ 

The conditional density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3(x+y)}{4})}{3{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(x+y)}{4{y}^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $0<x\le 2y,\,0<y\le 1.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=0.$ 

Now, substituting $y=1$ into the expression for ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y),$ we get

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)=\frac{(x+1)}{4}.
$$

Therefore, using the definition of the conditional expectation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=1] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\cdot \frac{(x+1)}{4}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}+x)\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(\frac{8}{3}+2)-0] \\  & =\frac{7}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the conditional expected value $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=1].$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional expected value of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ is a function of $y.$ 

The conditional density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(1+y-x)}{2y},\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le x\le 2y,\,0\le y\le 1.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=0.$ 

Now, substituting $y=1$ into the expression for ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y),$ we get

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)=\frac{(2-x)}{2}.
$$

Therefore, using the definition of the conditional expectation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=1] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\cdot \frac{(2-x)}{2}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(2x-{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[{x}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[(4-\frac{8}{3})-0] \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2+y-x}{3}, & 0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{5-2x}{6}, & 0\le x\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $X$ are shown above. Find the conditional expected value $\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=1].$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional expected value of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

$$
\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=x]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}y.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=x]$ is a function of $x.$ 

The conditional density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2+y-x}{3})}{(\frac{5-2x}{6})} \\  & =\frac{2(2+y-x)}{5-2x},\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)=0.$

Now, substituting $x=1$ into the expression for ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x),$ we get

$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,1)=\frac{2(2+y-1)}{5-2\cdot 1}=\frac{2(1+y)}{3}.
$$

Therefore, using the definition of the conditional expectation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=1] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,1)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot \frac{2(1+y)}{3}\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(y+{y}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}[(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3})-0] \\  & =\frac{5}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
